causal_seam: _candidate_progress_watchdog_script starts a setsid shim in background and immediately assumes its PID is a process-group ID. The watchdog terminates early while its target PID still belongs to the parent group: group-directed signal/probe misses the live shim, watcher exits, shim forms its group later, direct Bash stays blocked waiting, and original Python subprocess.run reaches its 15-second bound. Signal and group-aliveness paths must include the still-live direct worker PID before PGID readiness.

external_observation.method: private out-of-process ps PID/PPID/PGID/comm sampling at roughly 0.25-0.35 seconds; narrowly selected lsof PIPE endpoints only after slow watchdog case and with nonempty selected PID list

limits: The observation proves the ordering and inherited writer retention; it does not attribute the long Python shim initialization delay to a specific host subsystem. Raw PIDs and pipe identifiers remain private. No other run in the six-run campaign was started after the first original failure.

repair.behavior: Wait up to five seconds for background setsid shim PID to become its isolated process-group ID. The no-progress clock restarts only after group readiness. Startup termination trap cleans worker process/group, inherited pipes and watchdog state before the regular signal handler takes over. A never-ready group exits 125 with bounded cleanup. Ordinary TERM/grace/KILL logic remains unchanged.
repair.code_surface: bin/prime-claw::_candidate_progress_watchdog_script only; original 15-second test body, assertion, shell fragment and selection unchanged
repair.initial_rejected_attempt: Fallback to signaling the direct PID before PGID readiness made original assertions miss worker PID files and failed the focused gate (3 failed); discarded before the final repair.
repair.new_regression: test_candidate_progress_watchdog_terminates_before_setsid_group_exists delays the test-only setsid shim by three seconds and asserts watchdog returns 124 and reaps the shim; original tests unchanged.
